script.text: The day before the midterms, U.S. forces struck Iran. Is the war back on?

Three U.S. officials told CBS News that American forces carried out limited defensive strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. One official cited Iranian anti-aircraft missiles. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim they downed two U.S. drones. That is unverified.

The Wall Street Journal reports smaller U.S. strikes have gone on for weeks. Yet talks continue. Iran's foreign minister says Qatar-mediated negotiations are making progress, with no final result. Iran offers to reopen Hormuz if Washington meets its conditions.

Axios reports Israel's prime minister is pressing Trump to strike Iran right after the midterms. Trump, for now, wants talks to play out. Secretary of State Rubio said Saturday that Trump has made no decision.
Will the U.S. and Iran reach a deal this month? Yes or no?

upload.title: US Strikes Iran Before Midterms. Is the War Back On? #shorts
upload.description:
On Monday, November 2, U.S. forces carried out limited "defensive" strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz, three U.S. officials told CBS News; a U.S. official told AP the strikes hit Qeshm Island. One official cited Iranian surface-to-air missiles fired at U.S. assets. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say, via Tasnim, that they downed two U.S. drones south of Qeshm; this is unverified. The Wall Street Journal reports that smaller U.S. strikes on Iranian targets have continued for several weeks. At the same time, Qatar-mediated talks continue: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says they are making progress but have reached no final conclusion, and Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. meets its conditions. Axios reports that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing President Donald Trump to strike Iran immediately after the U.S. midterm elections on November 3, while Trump wants negotiations to play out for now. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Trump has made no decision on resuming military action. Most details come from officials and the warring parties and could not be independently verified.
